observations.firstImpressions: Before reading any source or technical output: a polished lantern-lit title screen, a short five-step skippable tour and a dense but readable market. The first screen offers a concrete 'Compare 2 Synth Saffron → Fogmouth' suggestion with the quote's age and a 'at 20% lower' downside. Every row has a sparkline, a +/- vs-usual percentage and a plain-language note. The map reads immediately as seven distinct islands joined by canals, with danger dots. The first five minutes felt like a modern, deliberate game rather than a spreadsheet.
observations.1_trade: At least five of six logged turns had a credible runner-up (decision log below), including closing turns on nights 28 and 29. Changes in cash, capacity and deadline changed the best choice. On night 3, ¤392 left me unable to afford Moon Ink, so I bought 8 saffron; late with ¤160k+, single Dreamsilk and Moon Ink units dominated. The 30-slot hold capped the pearl loop on nights 13–15, and the 45-slot upgrade enabled the 40-slot freight. Fleet windows forced 'sell now or miss the call'. The trade sheet quotes price impact precisely ('past 4, each one costs more. The last goes at ¤13,078'), the default quantity respects flat depth, and the default buy keeps a 15% reserve. Strongest counterevidence: late game collapses to 'buy as many of the widest-spread expensive good as depth allows'. Glowkelp and rain become filler, and the hold rarely binds once Dreamsilk and Moon Ink are affordable. I also sold 29 saffron through the depth warning for −¤569 (my error; the sheet warned me).
observations.2_routes: The map is spatial and every route card shows nights, a danger rating (1/5 to 4/5), the exact Gull Gang toll for the current purse and hold, services, and the best quote with its age and a suggested haircut. Port details show 'usually supplies/imports' habits and every quote's age. Competing routes compared: on night 1, Fogmouth (risk 4/5, saffron ¤1,635, fleet buyer scheduled) vs Orchid (risk 1/5, ¤1,157, 'buyer may be absent'); on night 28, Sluices (risk 3/5, silk ¤14,303) vs Orchid (risk 1/5, ¤11,702). Quote versus arrival, before the wireless: Fogmouth saffron N1 ¤1,635 → N2 ¤1,711; Fogmouth saffron 1n-old ¤1,711 → N4 ¤1,392 (−19%, inside the 'try 25% below' advice); Orchid Dreamsilk 5n-old ¤12,501 → N7 ¤13,958; Lanternquay Dreamsilk 3n-old ¤11.4k → N5 no dealers; Exchange Dreamsilk 5n-old ¤16.6k → N6 no dealers. After buying the wireless on N22: Orchid silk live ¤23,010 → N23 ¤22,969; Lanternquay ink live ¤17.3k → N25 ¤18,134; Exchange eels live ¤4,811 → N28 ¤3,713 (−23%); Saint Mire rain live ¤198 → N24 ¤132 (−33%, beyond the 'try 20% below' advice). Reliability is explainable from age labels, haircut advice and the 'buyer may be absent / fleet buyer scheduled' wording. Counterevidence: about 7 of roughly 35 targeted sales across both runs arrived to 'No dealers tonight', the haircut advice undershot twice, and one warning compared a Lanternquay buy with a ¤584 Saint Mire price while a 1n-old ¤1,662 Fogmouth quote existed. It was probably excluding the expiring fleet, but it read as confusing.
observations.3_economy: Debt is 6% compounding to night 10, 10% after, with a credit limit of ¤6,000 plus net worth. The vault pays 1.5% a night and only Lanternquay and the Exchange have branches. Copperhook sells hold racks 30→45 (¤2,500) and a twin-screw motor (¤4,500); the Exchange sells the wireless (¤6,000); Saint Mire sells weapons; any port sells ¤20,000 charters; Ysolde sells whispers. Consignments run from night 15: post ¤2,800, bonded freight ¤18k→¤42k. Two investment approaches gave useful options after the opening: (a) hold upgrade → bonded freight twice (+¤24k each); (b) the wireless, which turned a blind Dreamsilk guess into a confirmed ¤10.7k→¤22.9k trade (+¤86k). Vault deposits were a real decision because they cut toll exposure from ¤30k to ¤6k. Counterevidence and gaps: hold racks at ¤2,500 are an obvious buy; repaying debt early is an obvious default; I did not exercise charters, weapons or whispers. Default-strategy check (scripted, unmatched seeds): the harness policy bought the wireless on N4 and reached ¤324k net worth by N21 (seed 43, stalled there); the same policy on keyboard (seed 31) had ¤284 cash on N10 and ended at ¤246.5k; my personal run ended at ¤341k with the wireless bought on N22. Early wireless looks very strong, but I did not run a matched with/without-wireless test from the same state, so the 90 anchor's equivalent-state check is missing.
observations.4_risk: I met the Gull Gang ambush (run/fight/toll), the Tidewarden cutter (run/fight/bribe/searched: 'seize half of every cargo and any deliveries'), the gull purse thief (70% to keep vs certain loss), flotsam (80% cargo vs 5–10% hull), Grandmother Wick's gamble (40% for 2.5×), courier jobs and lamplighter rumours. Outcomes matched offers exactly. N28 toll offer '¤6,157 cash · 12 Bottled Rain, 1 Synth Saffron' → taken exactly that. Voyage 2 N3 Tidewarden run-fail offer 'rakes your hull and grab 12% of each cargo' → −9% hull, 1 rain, 1 saffron; the next try escaped. Recovery after material hits: N5–6 Dreamsilk with no buyers at Lanternquay or the Exchange → partial debt repayment of ¤6,000 plus a re-route to Orchid sold it at ¤13,958; N9 eel surge collapse (bought ¤3,894, Orchid fell to ¤2,737) → carried to Saint Mire, took −¤2,547 and redeployed into saffron and pearls. Toll stakes scale with purse and are shown on the route card, so vaulting cash is a real mitigation. Counterevidence: the gull purse thief fired 6 times in about 38 voyages and flotsam 6 times; both became rote.
observations.5_pacing: The opening was debt-driven: a ¤2,500 purse, ¤6,000 at 6% due N10 and cheap goods. Growth had fleet loops, consignments from N15 and upgrades. The close had freight windows, vault protection, final-night routing and 'arrival after the closing night misses the call'. No two consecutive nights lacked a meaningful choice. On waypoint nights of 2-night routes I still traded at Lanternquay. Deadline-shaped final decisions: N28 vault ¤85k and run saffron and silk to the Sluices vs a safer Orchid; N29 buy 45 pearls (avg ¤378) for an N30 Exchange sale at ¤673 avg vs stay. The ending names the rank (Lantern Broker), the next rank gap ('¤58,713 short of Tide Baron') and reconciles: cash ¤124,444 + vault ¤216,843 + cargo ¤0 − debt 0 = ¤341,287. Debt interest ¤2,109, vault earned ¤11,843 and losses ¤8,741 are all consistent with play. Counterevidence: the snowball is steep (¤54k on N19 → ¤341k on N30) and the late game has no pressure beyond tolls.
observations.6_replay: Voyage 2 reshuffled the fleet calendar (rain at Saint Mire N1–4 and saffron at Fogmouth N5–8, vs saffron at Fogmouth N1–4 in voyage 1), prices and events, and brought a different encounter (the Tidewarden cutter). Early adaptation: rain to the Saint Mire fleet, then saffron. Later adaptation: a second Saint Mire → Fogmouth saffron loop during the N5–8 call, with debt repaid on N8 instead of N10. Voyage 2 reached ¤25.7k net worth by N10 vs ¤9.5k in voyage 1. Another approach worth trying: buy the wireless and hold racks before N10 and chain fleet calls with live quotes, or use credit for early Moon Ink. Counterevidence: the map, district identities and two calendar slots (Glowkelp at Copperhook N9–12, pearls at Orchid N13–16) were identical in both voyages.
observations.7_onboarding: Visible cues explain the first buy (the comparison card plus the sheet: price each, total, purse after, hold after, depth, reserve), the first voyage (route card: nights, danger, toll), and the first sale (profit vs average paid). Unexpected prices are explained by bulletins ('Tidewardens raided the Clockwork Eels stalls at Orchid Terraces'), 'Fading surge' and 'Glut' tags, and 'No dealers tonight'. Constraints are shown in place: 'Above your purse', 'Hold full', 'Free 40 hold slots to take this', 'must be repaid by night 10', and the credit limit text. After the tour I never needed the help screen. Counterevidence: text density is high on the phone; 'best recent sale quote' wording confused me once; a returning player gets no tour on the second voyage (sensible).
observations.8_input: Touch: a full 30-night run plus a second voyage at 390x844 in Playwright WebKit, with real touchscreen taps and typed quantities, no blocking. The phone audit on market, map, trade sheet, a choice modal and the ending screen found 0 targets under 44 px, 0 gaps under 8 px, 0 text under 15 px, 0 contrast failures under 4.5:1 (approximate), 0 inputs under 16 px and no horizontal overflow. Keyboard at 1280 (my Chromium spot checks): Tab reaches Cast off, the tour's Skip, goods rows, the trade sheet (Buy/Sell, quantity input, confirm), HUD explainers, the menu and map nodes (aria 'Orchid Terraces, danger 1 of 5. Press 3.'), all with a 2 px amber outline or a white ring on SVG nodes. Enter on a node moves focus to 'Sail here'. Number hotkeys pick districts. Event modals receive focus ('1 Continue'). Escape skips the tour and closes sheets. Scripted keyboard-play (seed 31) reached settlement with 2,069 Tab presses and 0 pointer events. Reduced motion collapses all animations (0 long animations under reduce). Non-colour cues: signed percentages, Cheap/Pricey/Glut/Surge text tags, 'risk n/5' text alongside danger dots.
observations.9_world: Districts are clearly drawn and named, and each has its own voice: the Fogmouth lighthouse, a cathedral 'sunk to its belfry', the Copperhook cranes, a columned Exchange, Sluices pumps, Orchid hanging gardens. Characters include Marrow Quill, Pell the lamplighter, Madame Ysolde and Grandmother Wick. Actions I followed without the log: a buy (toast 'Loaded 2 Synth Saffron for ¤1,676', purse count-down, row highlight); a voyage (skiff animates along the lit canal, night counter advances, arrival card); an encounter (illustrated Gull Gang header, hull/boats/cargo-at-stake stats, explicit outcome card); and the ending (emblem, rank title and breakdown). The source defines 18 distinct synthesized cues (buy, sell, profit, travel, arrive, event, alarm, hit, shot, splash, escape, win, lose, bank, upgrade and more). The audio stand-in recorded 990 sounds started only after a touchend unlock and none while suspended. Mute kept the count at 252 across trades; unmuting resumed it (261). Routine actions are quick (one tap to open, one to confirm), and voyages can be skipped by tapping. Not judged: actual listening quality (no audio output in Windows WebKit). Counterevidence: repeated gull and flotsam events.
observations.10_reliability: Normal play: a full 30-night run plus 10 nights of voyage 2 in the phone harness with no page errors. The ledger survived reload (Lantern Broker ¤341,287 #1, then voyage 2 recorded as #2). Direct file:// boot offline: OK. Sandboxed iframe (allow-scripts only): booted, traded and sailed to N2 with no errors. localStorage getter throwing: game ran to N2 without errors. Corrupt JSON in the save, scores and settings keys: ledger shows empty and the game runs without errors. Additional adverse check: reload mid-run offers 'Continue voyage'. Zero non-file requests in every context. Single file of 267,386 bytes with the only URL being an inline data-URI favicon's SVG namespace. Every localStorage call sits inside try/catch with a memory fallback. Arithmetic checked: 8×¤1,392 = ¤11,136; debt 6,000 → 6,360 → 6,742 → 7,147 → 7,576 (6% compound); vault deposit ¤120,000 'earns tomorrow ¤1,800' (1.5%); both ending breakdowns reconcile (¤341,287 and ¤1,969 + ¤11,874 = ¤13,843; interest ¤9,024 − ¤6,000 = ¤3,024). Gap: one scripted harness run (touch-play seed 43) stalled on night 21 when Playwright waited for a visible 'Sell 7' button to become stable. I could not attribute this to the game: reduced motion disables all CSS animation, my manual taps never failed, and keyboard-play completed, so I treat it as a driver flake.

defaultStrategyCheck.method: tools/touch-play.cjs default policy (scripted; FAST and reduced motion; seed 43) and tools/keyboard-play.cjs (scripted; seed 31). The seeds do not match my personal runs, which were unseeded.
defaultStrategyCheck.results: Touch policy seed 43: bought the wireless N4, repaid N5, motor and hold N14; net worth about ¤324k by N21, when the driver stalled on a Playwright stability wait (no page errors). Keyboard policy seed 31: ¤284 cash on N10, ended at ¤246,510 (Canal Runner). Mine: ¤341,287.
defaultStrategyCheck.reading: A mechanical adjacent-port arbitrage policy with early wireless scores in the same range as careful play, and seed luck matters a lot. Trading decisions still drive the outcome; there is no bypass.

priorities: Make arrival risk easier to price: about 1 in 5 targeted sales met 'No dealers tonight', and the haircut advice undershot twice (−32% and −33% against 'try 20–25% below'). Show per-good dealer presence history or a probability on quotes, and recalibrate or explain the haircut, so being 'unlucky' feels like a readable risk.

Add pressure or texture to the late game: net worth snowballs from about ¤54k on N19 to ¤341k on N30 through single Dreamsilk and Moon Ink units, while low-value goods become filler. The hold racks (¤2,500) and early wireless (¤6,000) look close to automatic. Consider steeper depth for expensive goods, late sinks or threats that scale with wealth, and a matched test of the early-wireless line.

Vary repeated encounters and clarify one warning: the gull purse thief fired 6 times and flotsam 6 times in about 38 voyages. The 'Above the best recent sale quote' message compared a buy with a supplier's price while ignoring a fresher (expiring-fleet) quote; say which quotes it ignores and why.
limits: Touch was Playwright WebKit on Windows with an iPhone 13 profile at 390x844, not a physical iPhone: no safe-area insets, software keyboard, double-tap zoom or Safari toolbars.
No audio output: the harness's Web Audio stand-in only shows unlock policy, sound-start counts and mute behaviour. I judged distinct cues from the 18 named sfx calls in the source, not by listening.

Voyage 1 nights 1–10 used manual step-by-step taps at normal animation timing; from night 10 I set FAST=true and used a helper that sends real taps and typed quantities and prints visible text. All choices remained mine. Voyage 2 used FAST throughout.

Desktop keyboard checks: my own Chromium 1280x800 spot checks (title, tour, trade sheet, map, hotkeys, sail, event focus, Escape) plus one scripted keyboard-play completion (seed 31). I did not personally keyboard through settlement or do a mouse-only run; mouse paths were assumed from the shared click handlers.
No matched-seed comparison between my runs and the default policy, and no controlled equivalent-state test of early wireless or freight. This is why economy stays below 90.

Contrast and size audits are the harness's approximations; the in-voyage event modal at 390 was checked with `ui` (356x89 choices) but the formal audit ran on the abandon-confirmation choice modal, not on an ambush.
I read NOTES.md only after play, for brief compliance: 59 lines covering title, concept, how to play, decisions, testing and known issues. I read no other judging files, git history or prior scores.
One scripted touch-play baseline (seed 43) stalled on N21 waiting for element stability; I could not reproduce it by hand and did not investigate further.
Small personal mistakes affected my score (sold 1 silk instead of buying through my helper on N24; sold saffron past depth on N29). These are mine, not game defects; the UI disclosed both.
